examples.solution_text:
(a) Four right-angle marks give a rectangle. It has two pairs of parallel opposite sides, so it is also a parallelogram and a trapezium. All four sides equal is not given.
Quadrilateral, trapezium, parallelogram, rectangle.
(b) Four equal sides and four right angles give a square. It also has every property needed for the other names in the list.
Quadrilateral, kite, trapezium, parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle, square.
(c) Both names are guaranteed. A rectangle has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so it is a parallelogram too.

examples.question_text:
Say whether each statement is always true, sometimes true or never true. Give a reason.
(a) A square is a rhombus.
(b) A rectangle is a square.
(c) A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is a parallelogram.
(d) Which statement in (a)–(c) is always true?
examples.solution_text:
(a) Always true. Every square has four equal sides, which a rhombus requires.
(b) Sometimes true. A rectangle is a square when all four sides are equal. A rectangle $7\text{ cm}$ long and $4\text{ cm}$ wide is not a square.
(c) Never true. A parallelogram needs two pairs of parallel opposite sides.
(d) Statement (a). The reverse claim, that every rhombus is a square, is not always true because a rhombus need not have right angles.

examples.question_text:
Give the most specific name guaranteed in each case. Explain how the two descriptions work together.
(a) A quadrilateral is a rectangle and a kite.
(b) A quadrilateral is a parallelogram and a kite.
examples.solution_text:
(a) A rectangle has equal opposite sides and four right angles. The kite gives two pairs of equal adjacent sides. Together these make all four sides equal.
Square.
(b) Equal opposite sides from the parallelogram and equal adjacent pairs from the kite make all four sides equal.
Rhombus. Right angles are not given, so a square is not guaranteed.

examples.question_text:
Give the most specific name guaranteed by each description. Give a reason.
(a) A quadrilateral has four right angles and four sides of length $5\text{ cm}$.
(b) Quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $AB=AD=6\text{ cm}$ and $BC=CD=10\text{ cm}$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Square. It has both four equal sides and four right angles.
(b) Kite. $AB=AD$ and $BC=CD$ give two pairs of equal adjacent sides. The side lengths $6\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$ are different, so it is not a rhombus.

examples.question_text: Sketch a kite $PQRS$ with $\angle PQR$ and $\angle PSR$ both obtuse. Mark its two pairs of equal adjacent sides.

examples.derivation: (a) Four sides of 5 cm and four right angles satisfy the definition of a square. (b) AB=AD=6 cm and BC=CD=10 cm establish two pairs of equal adjacent sides, hence a kite. Since 6≠10, it is not a rhombus. Both tasks adapt Foundation question 2 using different values; no diagram is necessary.

The coordinates give PQ=PS=√10.44 and QR=RS=√5.44, establishing a kite with the indicated matching marks. At Q, vectors QP=(-3,-1.2) and QR=(2,-1.2) have dot product -4.56, giving an interior angle approximately 127.235°. Reflection gives the same angle at S. Both are obtuse. The authored arcs span approximately 127.235° inside the kite and agree with these angles. Labels and marks are black, and the completed sketch appears only in the solution. This adapts Foundation question 6(c).
